sentences.label: Lowering the chance
sentences.text: These add up independently, and these lower the chance steadily: a higher education level lowers the predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about 84% at 7 to about 34% at 13 on the 1-16 scale, and, through this sum alone, older age from about 81% at 22 to about 30% at 58 years and capital gains from about 62% at 0 to about 23% at 6849 US dollars (both also act through parts below); higher capital losses (about 62% at 0 to about 31% at 1887 US dollars) and longer working hours (about 70% at 24 to about 54% at 55 hours a week) lower it too.

Being a wife rather than a husband lowers it, through this sum alone, to about 39%; a highest education of 5th-6th grade lowers it to about 30% and 7th-8th grade to about 41%, an executive or managerial job to about 52% and working for the federal government to about 51%.

sentences.label: Raising the chance
sentences.text: Any marital status other than married (to a civilian, to a member of the armed forces, or with the spouse absent) raises it to about 87% and being a woman to about 73%; through this sum alone, a relationship in the household other than husband, unmarried or wife raises it to about 90%, being unmarried to about 82%, farming or fishing to about 85% and handling or cleaning to about 80% (relationship, occupation and country of birth also act through the parts below).

sentences.label: Country of birth
sentences.text: Through this sum alone, being born in Trinidad and Tobago raises it to about 92%, in Scotland to about 81% (the model has little data on this, n = 16) and in Puerto Rico to about 74%, while being born in Ireland lowers it to about 37% and in England to about 52%.

This part acts on 8609 of 39073 training people, 5807 of whom have an income of $50,000 or less; for the typical person it acts on (aged 57), the predicted chance is about 31% without it and about 50% with it.
Through it, age adds nothing until about 50 years, then raises a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) steadily, from about 62% at 22 to about 81% at 58 years.
Being born in Colombia raises it through this part to above 99%, and for people born in Colombia age works the other way, steadily, though their chance stays above 99%.
Across the whole model, the chance is lowest at about 50 years and higher either side, from about 81% at 22 to about 52% at 58 years.

Through this part, higher capital gains lower a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) steadily, from about 62% at 0 to about 46% at 6849 US dollars; across the whole model the fall is steadily from about 62% to about 14%, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.

This part acts on the 10067 people not living in a family, 9086 of whom have an income of $50,000 or less; for the typical person it acts on, the predicted chance is about 98% without it and about 94% with it.
Through it, not living in a family lowers a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about 62% to about 37%.

This part acts on the 2197 people whose occupation is missing, 1992 of whom have an income of $50,000 or less; through it, a missing occupation raises a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about 62% to about 80%.
A missing country of birth raises it from about 62% to about 72% for people whose occupation is known, but lowers it from about 80% to about 72% when the occupation is missing too.

parts.name: income_logit_root
parts.original_hypothesis: ROOT (supported). Output 0 = sigmoid(z), z = 1.399 + 48 direct input terms + 12 hidden readouts (9 child annotations); 52 of the 107 one-hot/standardized inputs are unconnected and listed here as zero-effect entries. Class 1 is the 76% majority (presumably <=50K), so negative weights push toward high income. The model is essentially a sparse logistic regression with one consequential nonlinearity. Direct edges carry logit SD 3.37 of 3.85 (mean-ablating them drops train AUC 0.910->0.518); all hidden readouts together carry SD 1.32 and mean-ablating every hidden unit costs only acc 0.856->0.838, AUC 0.910->0.895. The only nonlinearity that matters is age_late_career_hinge (4647): keeping it alone recovers acc 0.850 / AUC 0.904. It turns the direct age slope (-0.88) into a U-shaped age effect with its minimum at age z~0.8. The other children are lookups or affine relays: capital_gain_affine_relay steepens the capital-gain slope to -2.54/SD; relationship1_indicator (-1.03 for relationship:1), occupation0_country0_gate (+0.92 for occupation:0 unless native-country:0), occupation8_relays (+0.45) and occupation1_relays (+0.37) are category offsets; country32_affine_relay and the native-country:4 part of the age hinge memorise rare countries; occupation6_relationship1_gate is near-inert (<=0.10 logit); dead_relationship_chain (613->2245->8678->170) and node 2114 are identically 0 on every valid input. Children combine ADDITIVELY in the logit (each child exit has one readout edge into node 0; no child feeds another). Largest exact logit-space attributions (mean |phi|, full train): relationship:0 0.82, education-num 0.72, marital-status:2 0.70, capital-gain 0.68, age 0.51, relationship:1 0.39, relationship:5 0.24, sex 0.23, occupation:8 0.21, hours-per-week 0.18.

parts.name: age_late_career_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: SUPPORTED: a single-knot age hinge giving a U-shaped (in class-1 logit) age effect. Below age z~0.80 the direct age term dominates (class-1 logit falls with age, i.e. the high-income share rises); above the knot 4647 reverses the slope to +0.65 per SD, so older workers drift back toward class 1, matching the empirical rate (minimum P(y=1) ~0.60 near z 0.8). native-country:4 (64 rows, standardized value 24.7) rides on the same unit as a large class-1 offset (memorisation of a rare category). EVIDENCE: Knot (for rows not in native-country:4, where nc4 = -0.041) at age z = 0.798. Active for 21.9% of those rows. Net age effect on logit = -0.881*age + 1.224*ReLU(1.249*age + 0.711*nc4 - 0.968): slope -0.881 below the knot and +0.648 above it. Logit contribution range [0, 24.36], SD 1.00 (the largest hidden-node contribution). The 64 native-country:4 rows (value 24.69) have 4647 ~ 16.6 (+20 logit), i.e. they are forced to class 1. line_plot on train (39,073 rows): exit 0 below z~0.8 then linear; scatter exit range [0, 19.9] (the top from nc4 rows). Empirical P(y=1) follows the same U: 0.999, 0.944, 0.664, 0.606, 0.597, 0.662, 0.764, 0.816. Mean-ablation of 4647: acc 0.8558->0.8436, AUC 0.9099->0.9009 (largest hidden-node effect).

parts.name: capital_gain_affine_relay
parts.original_hypothesis: SUPPORTED: affine relay. 1870 = ReLU(0.439*capital-gain + 0.850) never clips on train, so it is a linear rescaling of capital-gain that adds -0.702*cg - 1.359 to the logit and steepens the direct capital-gain term (-1.841) to a total slope of -2.54 per SD. No nonlinearity is used on the data domain (the knot sits at cg z = -1.94, below the data minimum -0.147). EVIDENCE: Always active on train (pre-activation in [0.786, 6.636], 39,073/39,073 rows), so on the data domain 1870 = 0.439*cg + 0.850 exactly and its logit contribution is -0.702*cg - 1.359 (range [-10.61, -1.26], SD 0.70). Combined with the direct edge (-1.841), the total capital-gain slope is -2.54 logit per SD, pushing toward class 0 (the 24% minority, presumably >50K). line_plot on train (39,073 rows): exit vs capital-gain correlation 1.000 (exactly linear over the observed range); 91.6% of rows sit at the zero-gain floor (cg z = -0.147). reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients
